text:
anita: Quick Q — I'm wiring a TF change: IRSA role for metrics-processor needs KMS decrypt grant. Trying to be strict: policy + key grant with aws:SourceAccount + aws:SourceArn condition matching the assumed-role ARN. Wanted a sanity check before I open the PR.

sam: paste the TF you have so far? especially the grant + policy bits.

anita: sure — here's the minimal bits I'm trying (sensitive bits redacted):

```hcl
data "aws_iam_policy_document" "irsa_kms" {
  statement {
    actions = ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"]
    resources = [aws_kms_key.metrics.arn]
    effect = "Allow"
    condition {
      test = "StringEquals"
      variable = "aws:SourceAccount"
      values = [var.aws_account_id]
    }
    condition {
      test = "StringLike"
      variable = "aws:SourceArn"
      values = ["arn:aws:sts::${var.aws_account_id}:assumed-role/${aws_iam_role.irsa_role.name}/*"]
    }
  }
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "metrics_irsa" {
  name = "metrics-irsa-grant"
  key_id = aws_kms_key.metrics.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.irsa_role.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}
```

anita: and the k8s annotation on the SA is `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: ${aws_iam_role.irsa_role.arn}`.

liz: looks mostly fine. nit: for grants you probably want the grantee_principal to be the assumed-role principal (sts ARN) rather than the role arn. Grants accept role or principal arn; using the role arn should still work but I've seen edge cases with session tags.

kevin: also think about session tag filtering instead of SourceArn if you're relying on the SA name. We sometimes require a session tag like `team=metrics` and then condition on `aws:PrincipalTag/team` or `aws:RequestTag/team` depending on how tokens are created. For IRSA we can pass session tags via the OIDC provider mapping if needed.

anita: hmm — is session tagging with IRSA stable? I thought only STS `TagSession` flow supports tags, and IRSA uses AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity which supports session tags if the provider allows it. I can add `sts:TagSession` in the policy call.

sam: right, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity supports passing session tags if the trust policy allows `sts:TagSession` and the role's `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` call includes tags. But k8s IRSA pods don't tag by default — you'd need kube2iam-like sidecar or the AWS SDK with web identity token that includes tags. That's often the friction.

liz: for a quick win, SourceArn matching is simpler but be explicit about the pattern. We match on `arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/metrics-irsa-*/*` in a few places. (Using `*` at the end to allow different session names).

anita: good point. Would you suggest updating the TF snippet to: `values = ["arn:aws:sts::${var.aws_account_id}:assumed-role/${aws_iam_role.irsa_role.name}/*"]` — that's what I have now.

kevin: that's fine, but add a note in the key policy to avoid wildcard principal escalation. E.g., key policy should limit principals to the role ARN and also include an explicit deny if `aws:SourceAccount` != our account.

anita: ok I'll add an explicit condition block in the key policy and a small deny clause. Also will switch the grant to use `grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.irsa_role.arn` for now and document the session tag follow-up.

sam: tiny nit: add `depends_on = [aws_kms_key.metrics]` to the grant resource to avoid TF race with key creation -> grant. We've hit that before in CI.

anita: good call. I'll add that.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline triggered by commit anita/infra/metrics-kms-grant (build #4532)

liz: thanks — if CI passes, can you open a PR and tag infra-team? I'll do a quick review for policy language.

anita: will do, thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin: one follow-up — can you include a smoke test (small k8s job) that mounts a secret encrypted with that key and runs `aws kms decrypt` via the pod? That saved us once.

anita: good idea, I'll add a smoke job to the PR that runs in a short-lived test namespace and reports decrypt success/failure.

sam: cool — LGTM after CI & smoke test.

anita: thanks everyone, I'll send the PR link when it's up.
